dimension: the identity-access MfaSecretCipher: the versioned MFA envelope over the root key ring
howToReproduce: Apply the `from` -> `to` replacement in `file`, run `command`, and observe the named case fail. Restore. Every entry runs on a laptop: neither adapter needs a container, a daemon or a database, which is what a keyless digest and an in-memory key ring are for.
notes: WHAT IS AND IS NOT A DIFFERENTIAL HERE, STATED PLAINLY. The canonical MFA envelope is NEW: the extraction source wrote format 2 — a raw key, no derivation, no salt, no version — and nothing has ever written this shape. So the frozen envelopes in `mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts` are a REGRESSION PIN, produced by this cipher, and calling them a differential would be the overclaim this repository has a rule about. The one real differential is on the READ side: `legacy-wire-vectors.ts`'s format-2 payloads came out of `internal-packages/tenancy-database/src/auth.ts` and cannot move with this code, and `mfa-refusal-reasons-collapsed` is killed through them.

THE FROZEN ENVELOPES ARE WHAT MAKE FIVE ENTRIES KILLABLE AT ALL. `mfa-aad-drops-the-version`, `mfa-hkdf-info-drops-the-version`, `mfa-hkdf-label-collides-with-credentials`, `mfa-salt-width-16` and `mfa-nonce-width-16` all move BOTH halves of a round trip together, so a suite built only on `open(seal(x)) === x` would report every one of them as passing. Against bytes that were written down, each is a tag failure.

ONE MUTATION SURVIVED ITS FIRST SWEEP AND IS RECORDED WITH THE CASE THAT WAS ADDED TO KILL IT. `mfa-field-count-check-removed` found that every refusal case in the file presented a payload whose FIRST field was wrong, so the marker check caught them all and the field count was never reached. The new case presents the right marker with too few fields and with too many; too many is the sharper half, because the extra field was ignored and the envelope OPENED.

A SECOND DEFECT WAS FOUND BY THE SWEEP'S MACHINERY RATHER THAN BY A MUTATION. The suite's tamper helper flipped the LAST base64url character of a field, and a 16-byte tag is 22 characters carrying 132 bits — the final one holds four meaningful bits and TWO the decoder discards. `A` -> `B` moved only a discarded bit, so the tag case failed outright and the salt and ciphertext cases PASSED for a reason that had nothing to do with the code. The helper now decodes, flips a byte, and re-encodes.

ONE ENTRY IS DECLARED UNFALSIFIABLE WITH A MEASURED REASON. `sealedUnderSameKeyVersion` compares a PUBLIC header — a literal marker and a key version the envelope carries in the clear — so its constant-time form protects no secret and no observation distinguishes it from `===`.

mutations.why: The associated data binds an envelope to its key version. Dropped on the READ side alone, every envelope this cipher ever sealed stops opening; dropped on both sides it would still fail the frozen vectors, which is why they exist.

mutations.why: With the version out of the AAD, an envelope re-labelled with another key version authenticates. Killed by the frozen envelopes, which carry the version inside bytes that cannot move with the code.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > the frozen canonical envelopes > opens the version-1 envelope it sealed at this format
mutations.why: The version is inside the key derivation, which is what makes a re-labelled envelope decrypt under a key that never sealed it. Killed by the frozen envelopes rather than by the round trip, which would move both halves together.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > the frozen canonical envelopes > opens the version-1 envelope it sealed at this format
mutations.why: The label space is the whole separation between this envelope and `secrets`' credential envelope: `platos:mfa-secret:v1:...` can never collide with `platos:credential-secret:v1:...`. A round trip cannot see this mutation at all — both halves move — and the frozen envelopes can.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > sealing > writes the widths format 1's descriptor pins
mutations.why: A narrower salt is a narrower per-envelope key derivation input, and it is the width `secrets/domain/envelope.ts`'s format-1 descriptor pins. Killed twice over: the width case reads the descriptor, and the frozen envelopes carry 32-byte salts.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > sealing > writes the widths format 1's descriptor pins
mutations.why: A GCM nonce of the wrong width changes the counter block and every stored envelope becomes unopenable.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > sealing > produces DIFFERENT ciphertext for the same plaintext, twice
mutations.why: A constant salt derives ONE key per root key rather than one per envelope, so two secrets share a key. The case observes that two seals of the same plaintext differ in the salt field, which a constant cannot satisfy.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > sealing > produces DIFFERENT ciphertext for the same plaintext, twice
mutations.why: A 12-byte GCM nonce reused under one key is a total break of the mode. The case observes two seals differing in the nonce field.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > sealing > names the ACTIVE version, and follows it when the ring rotates
mutations.why: Writing a constant version label means an envelope sealed under key 2 claims key 1, so it derives under one key and unseals under another — silent, permanent data loss on a write that reported success.

mutations.to: const version = state.value.presentVersions[0] as typeof state.value.activeVersion;
mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > sealing > names the ACTIVE version, and follows it when the ring rotates
mutations.why: `presentVersions` is sorted ascending, so this seals under the OLDEST key in the ring rather than the active one. A rotation would then never take effect, and the old key could never be retired.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > refusing > refuses a payload with the wrong marker
mutations.why: Without the marker, a three-field legacy column and a six-field canonical one are told apart by length alone, and a payload that happened to have six dot-separated fields would be decoded as canonical.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > refusing > refuses a payload with the RIGHT marker and the wrong field count
mutations.why: THIS ONE SURVIVED ITS FIRST SWEEP and the case that kills it was written afterwards. Every refusal case in the file presented a payload whose FIRST field was wrong, so the marker check caught them all and the count was never read. Too FEW fields then destructures `rawCiphertext` to undefined and is reported as a tag failure — a wrong reason for a wrong shape; too MANY is worse, because the extra field is ignored and the envelope OPENS.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > refusing > refuses a version that is not an integer literal
mutations.why: `Number(" 1 ")` is 1, so without the literal check a payload labelled ' 1' and one labelled '1' name the same key while being different strings — and the label is inside the HKDF `info`, so they do not derive the same key.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > refusing > refuses a tampered TAG rather than returning plaintext
mutations.why: The port's whole clause: an implementation MUST reject a tampered envelope rather than returning wrong plaintext. Returning the empty string hands `verify-mfa` a TOTP secret of length zero and turns an authentication failure into an authentication.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > refusing > refuses a payload with the wrong marker
mutations.why: Two guards returning the same code cannot be told apart. Collapsed, an operator whose column still holds a legacy format-2 envelope is told the bytes are corrupt — which is a key rotation they should not perform instead of a migration they should.

mutations.killedBy: src/mfa-secret-cipher.test.ts > the port on the adapter > is reachable by name and is not the AeadCipher
mutations.why: The composition root binds `keyring-envelope.mfaSecrets` BY NAME. Without the property the binding is `undefined` at runtime and `PORT_SATISFACTION`'s `KeyringEnvelopeAdapter["mfaSecrets"]` obligation is the compile-time half of the same claim.

declaredUnfalsifiable.why: MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and the reason is different from the one above: this helper compares a PUBLIC header — a literal marker and a key version an envelope carries in the clear — so there is no secret for a timing difference to leak and the constant-time form buys nothing an attacker could not read directly. It is written that way for uniformity with the comparison next door rather than for a property, no observation distinguishes the two, and recording that is more honest than counting it as a kill.
